rationale: Pulmonary blastoma (pneumoblastoma) is defined by WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed as a rare subtype of lung cancer (biphasic tumor of the lung); it is a bronchopulmonary parenchymal tumor and is not a tracheal entity. It is thus restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed defines pulmonary blastoma as a rare biphasic subtype of lung cancer arising in the lung; it is a bronchopulmonary tumor, not a tracheal one. Restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: Esthesioneuroblastoma arises from the specialized olfactory neuroepithelium of the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid region, and olfactory nerve; ectopic occurrence in paranasal sinuses other than the ethmoid is vanishingly rare. It is therefore restricted to nasal cavity, ethmoid sinus, and olfactory nerve, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary C310, frontal C312, sphenoid C313 sinuses and other cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Olfactory neuroblastoma (a synonym for esthesioneuroblastoma) arises from olfactory neuroepithelium in the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid, and olfactory nerve; ectopic paranasal-sinus (non-ethmoid) tumors are vanishingly rare. Restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary, frontal, sphenoid sinuses and non-olfactory cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Fluid overload-associated LBCL presents as serous body-cavity effusions without detectable tumor masses, lymphadenopathy, or organ involvement, occurring in the pleural (majority), pericardial, and peritoneal cavities. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380); peritoneum is not in the ceiling, and it does not involve the lung parenchyma, mediastinal tissue, bone marrow, spleen, or lymph nodes, so it is restricted to a proper subset.

rationale: A synonym for fluid overload-associated LBCL, which presents as serous effusions confined to body cavities (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal) without tumor masses or organ involvement. rationale: A uveal melanoma is by definition an intraocular melanoma of the uveal tract (choroid, ciliary body, iris) of the eye; it does not arise on lip, skin or scrotum, so it is restricted to the intraocular (choroid C693 / ciliary body C694) subset of the ceiling.
